items.title: Fuel pump impeller may swell and stall the engine
items.summary: The resin impeller in the fuel pump can deform and interfere with the housing; the engine could stop while driving. 7,052 vehicles worldwide.

items.title: Fuel pump failure (second campaign)
items.summary: Insufficiently dense resin in the pump can deform and cause failure and stalling. 21,353 vehicles worldwide.

items.title: Door harness wires may break (side and curtain airbags)
items.years: Built from start of production to 2 December 2020
items.summary: Repeated door opening can damage the harness so the side and curtain airbags may not deploy correctly. 32,800 vehicles worldwide.

timeline.change: Production starts at Suzuki's Kosai plant on 29 May; Japanese launch of the JB64 Jimny and JB74 Jimny Sierra on 5 July; European debut in Germany in October; South Africa in November
Fuel-pump recall covers cars built 9 May to 22 November 2018
UK's 1,200-car 2019 allocation sells out by December 2018, with waits of up to a year. Australia launches in January 2019
Passenger Jimny withdrawn from the UK in July over CO2; two-seat Jimny Commercial arrives from September. Door-harness airbag recall covers cars built up to 2 December 2020
Mexico launch in November; the first 1,000 reserved units sell out in three days
Maruti Suzuki starts Indian assembly for export in January. Australia adds the Lite grade in June, with the queue at up to 12 months
5-door JC74 revealed in India in January; Indian launch on 7 June; Australian Jimny XL from 5 December

Japan's 5-door Jimny Nomade launches on 30 January and orders are suspended after about 50,000 in four days. Australia pauses 3-door supply for new ADR rules in February. Jimny Commercial withdrawn from European sale
Australian Jimny XL stop-delivery from late July; sales resume 27 August after Suzuki confirms no safety or compliance issue
Nomade orders reopen in Japan on 30 January. Updated Australian 3-door adds adaptive cruise, lane-keep assist and front and rear parking sensors
The earliest JB74s (built from May 2018) turn 25 and become eligible for US import under NHTSA's 25-year exemption

identify.intro: The JB74 is still new and everywhere outside North America, so identification is mostly about kei versus Sierra, 3-door versus 5-door, and the European two-seat van.

items.head: JB64 or JB74
items.body: The Japanese kei JB64 has no wheel-arch extensions and tucked-in bumpers, is 1,475 mm wide and uses the 658 cc R06A turbo three. The JB74 has bolt-on flares, is 1,645 mm wide and uses the 1.5 K15B.

items.head: Model code
items.body: The model codes are JB64W for the kei car, JB74W for the Jimny Sierra and global 3-door, and JC74W for the 5-door.

items.head: 3-door or 5-door
items.body: The 5-door (Jimny XL in Australia, Nomade in Japan) has a 2,590 mm wheelbase versus 2,250 mm and is built only in India; the 3-door is built in Japan, and in India for some export markets.

items.head: Commercial version
items.body: UK and European Jimny Commercial vans have no rear seats and a partition behind the front seats. They were homologated as light commercial vehicles.

paragraphs: The fourth-generation Jimny has never been sold in the United States, and Suzuki hasn't sold cars here since American Suzuki's 2012 bankruptcy. It isn't certified to US safety or emissions standards, so it can't be imported as a new or late-model car.

The way in for older foreign cars, NHTSA's exemption for vehicles 25 or more years old (49 CFR 591.5(i)), runs from the date of manufacture. JB74 production began on 29 May 2018, so the earliest trucks become eligible in mid-2043, 2023-on 5-doors from 2048, and each truck on its own 25th birthday.

CBP's September 2022 Puerto Rico case shows what happens if you try sooner. A US citizen bought a 2022 Jimny in Mexico, where it has been sold new since November 2020, drove it across the border and shipped it to Puerto Rico. CBP seized it: DOT ruled it ineligible because it was 'less than 25 years old from the date of manufacture,' and EPA said it couldn't be certified because the Jimny isn't sold in the US. CBP said such vehicles 'must be brought into compliance, exported, or destroyed.' Until 2043, the legal small Suzuki for an American is a 25-year-old third-generation JB23 or JB43.
